input_prompt: Here is my ball-by-ball log for Overs 1-6 (18 balls faced): 0, 1, 4, 0, 0, 6 | 1, 0, 2, 0, 4, 0 | 0, 1, 1, 6, 0, 2. How did my powerplay go?
coach_response: Your scoring rate in the powerplay is strong (28 off 18, SR 155.56) with two sixes and two fours, which puts pressure on bowlers early. However, 8 dot balls out of 18 (44.4%) means you are either hitting boundaries or stalling—cutting just 2–3 dot balls into quick singles will push your impact even higher without extra risk. Drill: 18-ball powerplay simulation where every dot ball must be followed by an active gap-find single on the next ball.

input_prompt: Ball-by-ball sequence in Overs 7-12 against spin: 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1 | 0, 1, 0, 0, 2, 0. Why is my momentum stalling?
coach_response: Facing 12 balls for 5 runs (8 dot balls, 66.7% dots) against spin puts heavy pressure on your non-striker and forces risky slogging later. When the ball isn't in your boundary arc against spin, prioritize working it into soft pockets at cover, point, or mid-wicket for ones and twos rather than defending statically. Drill: 12-ball spin-rotation drill where your only goal is 6+ scoring shots (singles/twos) without hitting in the air.

input_prompt: My death-over bowling log (Over 19): 1, 4, 6, W, 1, 2. How should I evaluate this over?
coach_response: Getting a wicket in the 19th over is valuable, and 14 runs isn't catastrophic at the death, but conceding a four, a six, and zero dot balls shows your length became hittable between deliveries. After a boundary, reset immediately with a wide yorker or pace-off slower ball on a consistent line rather than repeating the same slot. Drill: 6-ball 'reset-after-boundary' bowling drill targeting wide yorker and slower cutter cones.

input_prompt: Look at my last 10 balls of an innings: 2, 4, 0, 1, 6, 1, 0, 4, 2, 1. What does this ball-by-ball pattern show?
coach_response: This is an ideal acceleration pattern: 21 runs off 10 balls (SR 210) with only 2 dot balls (20%) and zero consecutive dots. Notice how you backed up big hits (4 and 6) with ones and twos instead of going quiet—that keeps bowlers off balance. Drill: 10-ball finishing sequence where you alternate boundary intent with controlled singles/twos to keep strike moving.

input_prompt: In my opening spell (Over 1), my ball-by-ball log was: 0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 1. Good start or sloppy?
coach_response: 5 runs in the first over with 4 dot balls is a solid opening over—you built early pressure with three dots upfront. The single boundary suggests one ball drifted into the batter's zone, so focus on keeping that fourth-stump seam line consistent across all six balls. Drill: First-over simulation bowling 6 consecutive balls at top-of-off channel.

input_prompt: Chase situation: 12 balls left, 22 needed. Ball-by-ball so far in last 2 overs: 1, 0, 4, 1, 0, 2 (6 balls left, 14 needed). How should I play the final 6 balls?
coach_response: Needing 14 off 6 balls means you need roughly two scoring shots of 4/6 plus smart running—you cannot afford two dot balls in a row. Pick your strongest scoring zone for full or length balls, and convert any mishit or yorker into a hard-run single or two rather than forcing a wild swing. Drill: Last-over 6-ball chase drill starting from 14 needed with target hit/run execution.

input_prompt: My ball-by-ball log shows a wicket every time I hit two dot balls in a row: 0, 0, W. Why does that keep happening?
coach_response: Back-to-back dot balls build internal pressure, which often makes you play a forced or pre-meditated shot on the third ball against a delivery that doesn't deserve it. Reset mentally after two dots—look for a safe single or leave rather than chasing a boundary out of frustration. Drill: Two-dot reset drill where you must play a controlled defensive or single-run shot on ball 3.

input_prompt: Here is a full 24-ball middle-to-death spell for a leg-spinner: 1, 0, 6, 1, W, 0 | 0, 1, 0, 4, 1, 0 | 1, 0, 2, W, 0, 1 | 6, 0, 1, 1, 0, 4. Summary?
coach_response: 25 runs and 2 wickets in 24 balls (economy 6.25, 45.8% dots) is a strong spell for a leg-spinner—you attacked, took wickets, and kept the overall rate economical. Your main leak is giving up two sixes and two fours on flighted/fuller balls, so tighten your length slightly after getting hit for a boundary. Drill: 24-ball leg-spin spell drill tracking length consistency after any boundary ball.
